# package snmp

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-profinet/snmp"
```

Package snmp implements a read-only SNMPv1/SNMPv2c agent (RFC 1157, RFC 1901, RFC 3416) with the BER codec of its messages (RFC 3417) and helpers for the MIB modules a PROFINET device of conformance class B offers: the system, interfaces and snmp groups of MIB-II (RFC 1213, RFC 3418, RFC 2863) and the LLDP-MIB of IEEE 802.1AB-2005.

The agent answers GetRequest, GetNextRequest and GetBulkRequest from a [MIB](#type-mib) and refuses every SetRequest; it sends no notifications (traps). SNMPv3 and its user-based security model are not implemented: a v3 message is dropped and counted. The community string is the only access control, and it travels in clear text: run the agent on isolated networks only.

The agent serves on a net.PacketConn the caller opens (the operating system's UDP socket, or a netstack socket on a virtual network); it starts no goroutines of its own until [Agent.Serve](#func-agent-serve).

## Types

### type Agent

```go
type Agent struct {

	// lim guards the token bucket.

}
```

Agent is a read-only SNMPv1/v2c agent. Its methods are safe for concurrent use.

#### func NewAgent

```go
func NewAgent(conn net.PacketConn, owned bool, cfg Config) (*Agent, error)
```

NewAgent returns an agent that serves on conn once [Agent.Serve](#func-agent-serve) runs. With owned, Close closes conn.

#### func (Agent) Close

```go
func (a *Agent) Close() error
```

Close stops Serve and waits for it to return; with an owned connection it closes the connection. It is safe to call twice.

#### func (Agent) Handle

```go
func (a *Agent) Handle(b []byte) []byte
```

Handle processes one request datagram and returns the response to send, or nil when the request is dropped. Serve calls it for every datagram; it is exported for transports that are not a net.PacketConn. It does not apply the rate limit.

#### func (Agent) LocalAddr

```go
func (a *Agent) LocalAddr() net.Addr
```

LocalAddr returns the address of the agent's socket.

#### func (Agent) Serve

```go
func (a *Agent) Serve(ctx context.Context) error
```

Serve answers requests until ctx is done or the agent is closed; it returns nil after Close, ctx.Err() when ctx is done, and the error of the socket otherwise. Only one Serve runs at a time.

#### func (Agent) Stats

```go
func (a *Agent) Stats() Stats
```

Stats returns a snapshot of the counters.

### type Config

```go
type Config struct {
	// Community is the community string a request must carry;
	// required. It is compared in constant time.
	Community string
	// MIB is the tree the agent serves; required.
	MIB *MIB
	// MaxMessageSize bounds a response; zero means
	// DefaultMaxMessageSize, and values below MinMessageSize are
	// raised to it. A Get or GetNext whose response would be larger is
	// answered with tooBig; a GetBulk response is truncated.
	MaxMessageSize int
	// MaxRepetitions caps the max-repetitions of a GetBulkRequest; zero
	// means DefaultRepetitions.
	MaxRepetitions int
	// MaxBulkVarBinds caps the variable bindings of a GetBulk response;
	// zero means DefaultBulkVarBinds.
	MaxBulkVarBinds int
	// Rate and Burst limit the requests the agent processes: Rate per
	// second on average, Burst at once. Excess datagrams are dropped
	// and counted (Stats.RateLimited). Zero means DefaultRate and
	// DefaultBurst; a negative Rate disables the limit.
	Rate  float64
	Burst int
	// Logger receives diagnostics. nil logs nothing.
	Logger profinet.Logger
}
```

Config configures an [Agent](#type-agent).

### type LLDPRemote

```go
type LLDPRemote struct {
	// TimeMark is when the row last changed, in sysUpTime units
	// (hundredths of a second since the agent started); 0 when that is
	// not known.
	TimeMark uint32
	// LocalPortNum is lldpRemLocalPortNum: the local port (1 to 4096)
	// the neighbor was heard on.
	LocalPortNum int32
	// Index is lldpRemIndex (1 to 2^31-1): an agent should give each new
	// neighbor of a port the next number and keep it for as long as the
	// neighbor stays (IEEE 802.1AB LLDP-MIB, lldpRemIndex).
	Index int32
	// The remote system's information: lldpRemChassisIdSubtype,
	// lldpRemChassisId, lldpRemPortIdSubtype, lldpRemPortId,
	// lldpRemPortDesc, lldpRemSysName, lldpRemSysDesc.
	ChassisIDSubtype int32
	ChassisID        []byte
	PortIDSubtype    int32
	PortID           []byte
	PortDesc         string
	SysName, SysDesc string
}
```

LLDPRemote is a row of lldpRemTable, INDEX { lldpRemTimeMark, lldpRemLocalPortNum, lldpRemIndex }.

lldpRemTimeMark is a TimeFilter (RFC 2021): the table holds a row for every filter value up to the row's last change, so that a manager that reads with filter t sees the rows changed since t. The agent serves GetNext and GetBulk at filter 0, which lists every row once (a finite walk), and answers a Get of any filter value t: the row is there when t ≤ TimeMark.

### type MIB

```go
type MIB struct {

	// regs is sorted by prefix and replaced, not modified, by Add.

}
```

MIB is the tree of objects an [Agent](#type-agent) serves: subtrees, each with a provider that returns the instances under its prefix when a request reads it. Subtrees do not overlap; within the MIB they are kept in lexicographic order, so that GetNext and GetBulk walk the instances in the order RFC 3416 section 4.2.2 defines. A MIB is safe for concurrent use; objects can be added while an agent serves it.

#### func NewMIB

```go
func NewMIB() *MIB
```

NewMIB returns an empty MIB.

#### func (MIB) AddInterfaces

```go
func (m *MIB) AddInterfaces(fn func() []Interface) error
```

AddInterfaces adds ifNumber and the ifTable (RFC 2863 section 6) with the interfaces fn returns. Rows whose Index is below 1 are left out.

#### func (MIB) AddLLDP

```go
func (m *MIB) AddLLDP(local func() LLDPLocal, remote func() []LLDPRemote) error
```

AddLLDP adds the local system data and lldpRemTable of the LLDP-MIB with the values local and remote return; remote may be nil (no neighbors). Ports and rows with indexes out of their range are left out.

#### func (MIB) AddSNMPGroup

```go
func (m *MIB) AddSNMPGroup(fn func() Stats) error
```

AddSNMPGroup adds the snmp group (RFC 3418 section 2; the counters RFC 3418 marks obsolete as RFC 1213 section 6.11 defines them) with the counters fn returns, usually an Agent's Stats. snmpEnableAuthenTraps is disabled(2): the agent sends no traps.

#### func (MIB) AddScalar

```go
func (m *MIB) AddScalar(object OID, fn func() Value) error
```

AddScalar adds a scalar object: its single instance object.0 has the value fn returns. fn may return the zero Value when the object has no value at the moment.

#### func (MIB) AddSubtree

```go
func (m *MIB) AddSubtree(prefix OID, fn func() []VarBind) error
```

AddSubtree adds the instances fn returns, for example the rows of a table, under prefix. fn is called once for each request that reads the subtree; it returns the instances in any order, each with a name below prefix (other names, duplicates and values that cannot be encoded are ignored).

#### func (MIB) AddSystem

```go
func (m *MIB) AddSystem(fn func() System) error
```

AddSystem adds the system group (sysDescr to sysServices, RFC 3418 section 2) with the values fn returns.

### type Message

```go
type Message struct {
	Version   Version
	Community []byte
	PDU       PDU
}
```

Message is a community-based SNMP message (RFC 1157 section 4, RFC 1901 section 3).

#### func Decode

```go
func Decode(b []byte) (Message, error)
```

Decode decodes a message. A message whose version is not v1 or v2c is reported with a \*VersionError (and its version); one that does not decode with an error that matches profinet.ErrMalformed. A v1 Trap PDU, whose layout differs (RFC 1157 section 4.1.6), is returned with its type only. Decode accepts no octets after the message.

#### func (Message) AppendTo

```go
func (m *Message) AppendTo(dst []byte) ([]byte, error)
```

AppendTo appends the BER encoding of m to dst.

### type PDU

```go
type PDU struct {
	Type      PDUType
	RequestID int32
	// ErrorStatus and ErrorIndex for every type but GetBulkRequest.
	ErrorStatus ErrorStatus
	ErrorIndex  int32
	// NonRepeaters and MaxRepetitions for GetBulkRequest.
	NonRepeaters   int32
	MaxRepetitions int32
	VarBinds       []VarBind
}
```

PDU is a GetRequest, GetNextRequest, Response, SetRequest, GetBulkRequest, InformRequest, SNMPv2-Trap or Report PDU; they share one layout (RFC 3416 section 3). A GetBulkRequest carries non-repeaters and max-repetitions where the others carry error-status and error-index.

### type Stats

```go
type Stats struct {
	// InPkts counts the datagrams the agent processed (snmpInPkts).
	InPkts uint64
	// OutPkts counts the responses sent (snmpOutPkts).
	OutPkts uint64
	// InBadVersions counts messages of a version other than v1 and v2c
	// (snmpInBadVersions).
	InBadVersions uint64
	// InBadCommunityNames counts messages with a wrong community
	// (snmpInBadCommunityNames).
	InBadCommunityNames uint64
	// InBadCommunityUses counts requests the community does not allow
	// (snmpInBadCommunityUses); always zero: a SetRequest is answered
	// as read-only, not refused for its community.
	InBadCommunityUses uint64
	// InASNParseErrs counts messages that did not decode
	// (snmpInASNParseErrs).
	InASNParseErrs uint64
	// InGetRequests, InGetNexts and InSetRequests count the requests
	// of each type (snmpInGetRequests, snmpInGetNexts,
	// snmpInSetRequests); InGetBulks has no object of its own.
	InGetRequests uint64
	InGetNexts    uint64
	InGetBulks    uint64
	InSetRequests uint64
	// OutTooBigs, OutNoSuchNames and OutGetResponses count the
	// responses with tooBig, with noSuchName and every response
	// (snmpOutTooBigs, snmpOutNoSuchNames, snmpOutGetResponses).
	OutTooBigs      uint64
	OutNoSuchNames  uint64
	OutGetResponses uint64
	// SilentDrops counts requests whose tooBig response did not fit
	// either (snmpSilentDrops, RFC 3416 section 4.2.1).
	SilentDrops uint64
	// UnsupportedPDUs counts well-formed messages that are not requests
	// (responses, traps, informs, reports): an agent ignores them.
	UnsupportedPDUs uint64
	// RateLimited counts datagrams dropped by the rate limit.
	RateLimited uint64
}
```

Stats are the counters of an [Agent](#type-agent). The first ones are the objects of the snmp group (RFC 3418 section 2, RFC 1213 section 6.11); [MIB.AddSNMPGroup](#func-mib-addsnmpgroup) serves them.

### type Type

```go
type Type byte
```

Type is the BER tag of a value (RFC 2578 section 7.1, RFC 3416 section 3).

```go
const (
	TypeInteger          Type = 0x02
	TypeOctetString      Type = 0x04
	TypeNull             Type = 0x05
	TypeObjectIdentifier Type = 0x06
	TypeIPAddress        Type = 0x40
	TypeCounter32        Type = 0x41
	TypeGauge32          Type = 0x42
	TypeTimeTicks        Type = 0x43
	TypeCounter64        Type = 0x46
	TypeNoSuchObject     Type = 0x80
	TypeNoSuchInstance   Type = 0x81
	TypeEndOfMibView     Type = 0x82
)
```

The value types. Integer, OctetString, Null and ObjectIdentifier are universal types; IPAddress to Counter64 are the application types of SNMPv2-SMI (RFC 2578 section 7.1.5 to 7.1.10, tags \[APPLICATION 0] to \[APPLICATION 6]); NoSuchObject, NoSuchInstance and EndOfMibView are the exceptions of a v2c response, implicitly tagged NULLs \[0], \[1], \[2] (RFC 3416 section 3).
